characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: room temperature; initial strain rate 10^-3 s^-1; averages of three measurements per material state
characterization_methods.purpose: mechanical screening of yield strength, ultimate tensile strength, and total elongation

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: rolling plane of samples ground to a thickness of 1 mm

characterization_methods.key_findings: No cracks, pores, or macrosegregations in the final materials; as-cast coarse dendritic microstructure became fully recrystallized (~20 μm grain size) after hot rolling and water quenching.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: cross-sectional areas in the plane perpendicular to the rolling direction

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: System modified to synthesize five different alloys in one operation using five Cu molds moved stepwise inside the furnace; molds successively filled with melt from a 4-kg ingot; after each cast the remaining melt composition was adjusted by charging Al through an air lock.
10 × 50 × 130 mm³-sized blocks hot rolled into 2 ± 0.1 mm thick and ~500-mm-long sheets.
After reheating and water quenching, sheets were cut perpendicular to the rolling direction into sets of nine segments (2 × 60 × 55 mm³) for each alloy composition.
Aging temperatures of 450 °C, 500 °C, 550 °C and 600 °C for 0 h, 1 h, and 24 h were applied; scales were removed from surfaces by low-pressure, fine-grit sandblasting after the heat treatments.

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: All plotted values represent averages of three measurements for every material state.
measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: tensile specimens prepared from 2 × 60 × 55 mm³ segments by package spark erosion

structures.overall_structure: Fully recrystallized single-phase austenite (fcc) microstructure with a grain size of ~20 μm and some retained Mn microsegregations.

unmapped_findings: For the Al-free ternary Fe-30Mn-1.2C reference material, aging leaves the yield strength virtually unchanged relative to the as-homogenized state (360 MPa YS, 830 MPa UTS, 77% TE), increases hardness slightly, but reduces UTS and TE; embrittlement becomes most apparent for long aging times (24 h) and higher temperatures (>500 °C). No exact numeric YS/UTS/TE values are printed in the text for the specific 500 °C/1 h aged condition, so only these qualitative trends are recorded for this sample.

This sample is the Al-free (x = 0 wt.% Al) reference ternary Fe-30Mn-1.2C composition of the Fe-30Mn-1.2C-xAl (wt.%) RAP screening; unlike the 8 wt.% Al variant, no κ-carbide (L′1₂, (Fe,Mn)₃AlC) strengthening is expected upon aging because κ-carbide formation is promoted by Al additions.

The paper presents a temperature-sensitive dislocation-density-based constitutive model for single-phase low-density TWIP (SIMPLEX) steels, the alloy class to which this Fe-30Mn-1.2C sample belongs; however, the model validation shown in Fig. 7 uses a Fe-22wt.%Mn-0.6wt.%C model TWIP alloy, and no sample-specific simulation of Fe-30Mn-1.2C is reported for this sample.
